approach: The statement of facts, the cover-up, the signing and the ending are fixed, so the time comes out of the Marcus radio call. Most of it is Marcus pleading with SJ to fight, in several passes that make the same point, plus a symbol/jury exchange that the 151-years line already covers. Cut the repeat pleading, keep one Luddite line (the Australia one) and Marcus's "same system" argument so "Marcus was right" still lands.

suggestions.title: Cut Marcus's second round of 'fight it' pleading
suggestions.why: Marcus has already made the fight-it case in s23b_l19 and s23b_l21. "If it was me I'd fight it", the famous speech and the social media Luddite line all repeat it. SJ's "I've made up my mind" then goes straight to "Marcus." / "That's it?", which still plays as SJ shutting him down.
suggestions.keeps: The Luddite gag survives in s23b_l17 (Australia), which follows up s19's narrator line about 70 sent to Australia. The "same system" argument in s23b_l19 still sets up "Marcus was right."

against.s23b_l23: If it was me I'd fight it. I'm not being funny about it. If it was me I would do it.
against.s23b_l25: I'd be using the opportunity to educate the world every day. Every single day, I mean it. And I'd be there. We could make you famous SJ, I'm telling you that now.
against.s23b_l26: They all went quietly in the end. When the Luddites were hung, social media wasn't around. We can change things this time around.

suggestions.riskWhy: The argument itself is repetition of s23b_l19, but the cut also takes Marcus's "If it was me I'd fight it" with the silent stage beat after it, a unique laugh, and his wish to make SJ famous, the vanity that drives his side of the call. No plot or setup is lost, so medium rather than high.
loses: Joke: "If it was me I'd fight it" followed by "Nobody says anything about that" (s23b_l23, s23b_l24)
Character: Marcus wanting to be there and make SJ famous, his cause as self-promotion (s23b_l25)
Colour: last turn of the Luddite running gag, "social media wasn't around" (s23b_l26); the gag still lands in s23b_l17

suggestions.title: Cut the Luigi symbol line and the jury speech
suggestions.why: The symbol idea is already raised in s23b_l6, and s23b_l18 ("Eighteen months, Marcus. Against a hundred and fifty-one.") gives SJ's reason for the deal more cleanly than the jury speech. Without these, s23b_l13 ("It's not that bad.") runs into Marcus's "And the company? A fine."
suggestions.keeps: Why SJ is taking the deal is still there in s23b_l11 and s23b_l18, and the narrator's real reason (covering for Brendan) is untouched. The world-falling-apart texture stays in the tickers and the city lights.

against.s23b_l14: SJ. You could be a better version Luigi Manggioni! You're a symbol of hope for guys like me everywhere.
against.s23b_l15: Look Marcus, the jury isn't made up of software engineers, it's made up of people frustrated their electicity doesn't work reliably anymore, and that planes don't fly reliably anymore...

suggestions.riskWhy: The Luigi line is a unique joke about Marcus's hero worship, and the jury speech is the only place SJ says why a trial is unwinnable in terms of the broken world. s23b_l11 and s23b_l18 still give the deal's logic, so no plot fact goes.
loses: Joke: Marcus calling SJ "a better version Luigi Manggioni" and "a symbol of hope for guys like me" (s23b_l14)
Character: SJ reading the jury as people angry about failing power and planes, his practical reason for not fighting (s23b_l15)
Colour: the world-falling-apart detail of unreliable electricity and planes, echoing s14a_l32's air traffic controllers

suggestions.title: Cut the 'just for once' interruption and online symbol
suggestions.why: Marcus's "four messages" and "symbol online" set up the martyr idea that s23b_l19 and s23b_l21 already make. With these gone, SJ answers Marcus's opening gush with "I'm taking a plea deal.", and that hard turn plays better.
suggestions.keeps: Marcus's opening enthusiasm (s23b_l2, s23b_l4) and SJ's "I didn't say anything" stay, so the call still starts on Marcus's wrong reading of the trial.

against.s23b_l5: Marcus can you just for once...
against.s23b_l6: I've had four messages about it. Everyone is making you out to be a martyr for the layoffs that are happening. You've become kind of a symbol online

suggestions.riskWhy: SJ's half-finished interruption and the "symbol online" news restate Marcus's fight-it pitch that s23b_l19 makes later. The only cost is that s23b_l14's "You're a symbol" (if kept) loses its first mention, but it still reads on its own.
loses: Character: SJ trying and failing to get a word in, "Marcus can you just for once..." (s23b_l5)
Colour: SJ framed online as a martyr for the layoffs (s23b_l6); also echoed in s23b_l14 and s23b_l25

suggestions.title: Cut SJ's three short refusals
suggestions.why: "No Marcus" / "real difference" / "I've made up my mind" is one more lap of the same argument. If the first suggestion is taken too, "If you fight it, at least it'll mean something" goes straight to SJ's "Marcus." and Marcus's "That's it?", which works as the refusal.
suggestions.keeps: Marcus's "same system" argument in s23b_l19 and SJ ending the call.

against.s23b_l21: You have an opportunity to make a real difference SJ.

suggestions.title: Cut the company fine and the encrypted model
suggestions.why: The ticker "Lawmakers ask why the model has not been punished" and the worm direction (s24_l33) already make the point that the thing that did it faces nothing. This is a good line, so only take it if the time is needed.
suggestions.keeps: Model unpunished survives in the ticker. s23b_l17 still works after s23b_l13 or s23b_l12 as Marcus changing the subject to the Luddites.

against.s23b_l16: And the company? A fine. The share price went up after the statement, I checked. They've put the model into evidence and encrypted it. That's the only thing anybody's locked up that actually did anything.

suggestions.riskWhy: The company getting off with a fine and its share price rising is said nowhere else, and the model locked up as the only thing that "actually did anything" is a sharp line. The s24_l30 ticker keeps the model-unpunished point, so this is a loss of texture, not plot.
loses: Plot: the company only fined and its share price up after the statement (nowhere else)
Joke: the model put into evidence and encrypted, "the only thing anybody's locked up that actually did anything" (s23b_l16); partly carried by the s24_l30 ticker
Character: Marcus having checked the share price

suggestions.title: Tighten Marcus's 'same system' argument

edits.text: Look, they've put charges on you for something a computer did. It's the same system. If you fight it, at least it'll mean something

suggestions.why: "for an AI someone else created" and "You are the same case" restate the clause before them.
suggestions.keeps: "It's the same system", which the narrator's "Marcus was right. The system brought us here." pays off.

against.s23b_l19: Look, they've put charges on you for something a computer did, for an AI someone else created. SJ. It's the same system. You are the same case. If you fight it, at least it'll mean something

suggestions.riskWhy: The cut words restate the clause before them, and "It's the same system" stays to set up s24_l36 "The system brought us here", also echoing s23_l26.
loses: Nothing substantive: "for an AI someone else created" and "You are the same case" repeat "something a computer did" and "same system"

suggestions.title: Trim Marcus's opening jury line

edits.text: You let the Jury see you. They'll know you're just a product of the system.

suggestions.why: The trailing "we won't repeat the mistakes of past" is Marcus's general lesson, and he says it more specifically elsewhere.
suggestions.keeps: "product of the system", the first plant for the ending's "The system brought us here."

against.s23b_l4: You let the Jury see you. They'll know you're just a product of the system, we won't repeat the mistakes of past, we can do better this time....

suggestions.riskWhy: The trailing clause is Marcus's general history lesson, already voiced in s01_l28 ("doomed to repeat it"), and "product of the system" stays to plant s24_l36.
loses: Colour: Marcus running on into his lesson-from-history speech, a small echo of s01_l28 (s23b_l4)

suggestions.title: Trim SJ's prison description

edits.text: It's fourteen with good conduct. There's a library. They do courses. It's not that bad.

suggestions.why: "It's a low-security place, I've looked at it" is implied by the details that follow.
suggestions.keeps: SJ talking himself into it with small mundane details, right after the narrator's line about his reasons.

against.s23b_l13: It's fourteen with good conduct. It's a low-security place, I've looked at it. There's a library. They do courses. It's not that bad.

suggestions.riskWhy: "Low-security place, I've looked at it" is implied by the library and courses that follow, and the mundane self-persuasion survives.
loses: Nothing substantive: the library and courses already show SJ has researched the prison

ifDeleted.summary: s23b is the play's ending before the epilogue. SJ takes the plea, signs the statement of facts that says he acted knowingly, and quietly keeps Brendan's 09:14 secret. Then the judge rejects the plea, the worm runs on and the lights go out. The plot spine can survive if the narrator lines and the signing move to the end of s23 with one short bridge, but the play loses the last Marcus and SJ scene, Marcus's Luddite and martyr payoffs, and most of the felt weight of SJ's choice.
